nodes.label: Model weights
nodes.description: The learned numbers that make up a trained model. They occupy most of a deployment's VRAM and are what you actually download.

nodes.label: Parameter count
nodes.description: How many learned values a model has. The headline number in a model's name, and the first input to every memory calculation.

nodes.label: Mixture of experts
nodes.description: An architecture where only part of the network runs on each token. Memory scales with total parameters, speed with active ones.

nodes.label: Active parameters
nodes.description: The parameters actually used on a given token. What predicts speed in an MoE model, where total count predicts memory instead.

nodes.label: Token
nodes.description: The unit a model reads and writes. Context window size, memory use, throughput, and cost are all counted in tokens.

nodes.label: Tokenizer
nodes.description: Software that turns text into token IDs and back. Its vocabulary decides how many tokens any given input costs you.

nodes.label: Context window
nodes.description: The maximum tokens a model can process in one request. Longer contexts cost KV cache memory, which costs concurrency.

nodes.label: GPU
nodes.description: The accelerator model inference runs on. Chosen for memory capacity and bandwidth at least as much as for arithmetic speed.

nodes.label: VRAM
nodes.description: The memory attached to a GPU. Weights, KV cache, activations and runtime overhead all have to fit inside it.

nodes.label: HBM
nodes.description: High Bandwidth Memory. The stacked memory on data center GPUs, and the reason their bandwidth is measured in terabytes per second.

nodes.label: Memory bandwidth
nodes.description: How fast a GPU can read its own memory. The ceiling on decode speed, because generating each token re-reads the whole model.

nodes.label: Memory bound
nodes.description: A workload limited by how fast memory can be read, not by arithmetic. Decode is memory bound, which explains most of its behaviour.

nodes.label: Compute bound
nodes.description: A workload limited by arithmetic capacity rather than memory speed. Prefill is compute bound, which is why long prompts are slow.

nodes.label: CUDA
nodes.description: NVIDIA's GPU computing platform. The layer every inference engine sits on, and most of why NVIDIA hardware is the default.

nodes.label: GPU utilization
nodes.description: The percentage of time a GPU has work resident. A high number does not mean the card is doing useful work efficiently.

nodes.label: Precision
nodes.description: The number format used to store weights and do arithmetic. It sets bytes per parameter, and so how much memory a model needs.

nodes.label: FP8
nodes.description: An 8-bit floating point format with native support on Hopper-class GPUs and newer. Half the memory of BF16, modest quality loss.

nodes.label: Quantization
nodes.description: Storing weights at lower precision to cut memory. Frees VRAM for KV cache, speeds up decode, and costs some accuracy.

nodes.label: VRAM budget
nodes.description: The accounting that decides whether a deployment works — weights plus KV cache plus activations plus overhead, against the card.

nodes.label: CPU offload
nodes.description: Moving part of a model into system RAM when it will not fit in VRAM. Makes the impossible possible and the fast slow.

nodes.label: OOM
nodes.description: Out of memory. The failure when a workload needs more VRAM than is free — usually under load rather than at startup.

nodes.label: Inference engine
nodes.description: The software that loads a model and serves requests against it. Where batching, KV cache management and scheduling actually live.

nodes.label: vLLM
nodes.description: The most widely used open-source LLM inference engine. Introduced PagedAttention, and made continuous batching standard.

nodes.label: Forward pass
nodes.description: One run of data through the model to produce output. The unit of work every inference metric is ultimately counting.

nodes.label: Prefill
nodes.description: The stage that processes input tokens. Compute bound, parallel across the whole prompt, and what time to first token measures.

nodes.label: Decode
nodes.description: The stage that generates output one token at a time. Memory bound, sequential, and what sets the pace of a streamed response.

nodes.label: Streaming
nodes.description: Sending tokens to the client as they are generated. Changes perceived speed without changing throughput at all.

nodes.label: OpenAI-compatible API
nodes.description: An inference API following OpenAI's request and response shapes. The de facto standard that makes engines and providers swappable.

nodes.label: Latency
nodes.description: How long an operation takes. For inference it decomposes into stages, and knowing which one dominates is what makes it fixable.

nodes.label: TTFT
nodes.description: Time to first token. Everything before generation starts — queueing, scheduling and prefill — and what interactivity feels like.

nodes.label: TPOT
nodes.description: Time per output token. The pace of generation once it has started, and what a streamed response feels like to read.

nodes.label: Throughput
nodes.description: How much work a deployment completes per unit time — usually total tokens per second across every in-flight request.

nodes.label: Tail latency
nodes.description: What the slowest requests experience. Averages hide it, and it is usually the number your users are actually complaining about.

nodes.label: Goodput
nodes.description: Throughput that also meets your latency targets. The honest capacity number, since work delivered too late has no value.

nodes.label: KV cache
nodes.description: Stored attention state for tokens already processed. It makes generation linear instead of quadratic, and it eats leftover VRAM.

nodes.label: KV cache capacity
nodes.description: How much cached attention state the free VRAM can hold. The real ceiling on concurrency, and the number to size a deployment on.

nodes.label: PagedAttention
nodes.description: Allocating the KV cache in small fixed blocks instead of one contiguous reservation per request. Recovers most of the wasted memory.

nodes.label: KV cache eviction
nodes.description: Reclaiming cached attention state when memory runs out. The engine's alternative to failing, and it costs recomputation.

nodes.label: Prefix caching
nodes.description: Reusing cached attention state across requests that share a prompt beginning. Turns repeated prefill into a lookup.

nodes.label: KV cache quantization
nodes.description: Storing cached attention state at lower precision. Buys concurrency directly, and is a separate decision from quantizing weights.

nodes.label: Batch size
nodes.description: How many sequences the engine processes in one step. The main lever on the throughput-versus-latency trade, and mostly automatic now.

nodes.label: Continuous batching
nodes.description: Letting requests join and leave the running batch as they arrive and finish, instead of processing fixed groups together.

nodes.label: Chunked prefill
nodes.description: Splitting long prompt processing into pieces so it interleaves with generation instead of stalling everyone else's stream.

nodes.label: Speculative decoding
nodes.description: Guessing several tokens with a cheap model and checking them all in one pass. Trades spare compute for lower latency.

nodes.label: Model parallelism
nodes.description: Splitting one model across several GPUs so it fits or runs faster. The umbrella term for tensor, pipeline and expert parallelism.

nodes.label: Tensor parallelism
nodes.description: Splitting each layer's matrices across GPUs so they compute one token together. Buys capacity and speed, costs communication.

nodes.label: Pipeline parallelism
nodes.description: Splitting a model into sequential stages of layers, one per GPU. Cheap on communication, but stages idle unless kept fed.

nodes.label: Data parallelism
nodes.description: Running whole copies of a model on separate GPUs and spreading requests between them. Buys throughput, never capacity.

nodes.label: Expert parallelism
nodes.description: Distributing an MoE model's experts across GPUs. Maps to how the model actually computes, but load depends on routing.

nodes.label: NCCL
nodes.description: NVIDIA's library for GPU-to-GPU collective communication. What tensor parallelism actually runs on, and a common failure point.

nodes.label: NVLink
nodes.description: NVIDIA's direct GPU-to-GPU interconnect. An order of magnitude faster than PCIe, and what makes tensor parallelism practical.

nodes.label: RDMA
nodes.description: Letting one machine read another's memory without involving either CPU. What makes multi-node GPU work viable at all.

nodes.label: Communication overhead
nodes.description: Time distributed GPUs spend exchanging data instead of computing. The tax that decides how far a model can usefully be split.

nodes.label: Endpoint
nodes.description: The network address requests are sent to. The stable thing clients know about, decoupled from the workers behind it.

nodes.label: Worker
nodes.description: One process with the model loaded, serving requests. The unit that gets created, destroyed, and billed.

nodes.label: Queue depth
nodes.description: How many requests are waiting rather than running. The earliest honest signal that capacity is short.

nodes.label: Concurrency
nodes.description: How many requests a deployment is processing at once. The dial connecting KV cache memory to throughput, latency, and cost.

nodes.label: Load balancing
nodes.description: Choosing which worker serves each request. Round-robin is wrong for inference, because requests vary enormously in cost.

nodes.label: Backpressure
nodes.description: Rejecting or slowing work when a service is full. Failing fast beats accepting requests you will serve too late to matter.

nodes.label: Health check
nodes.description: A probe asking whether a worker is working. Conflating "alive" with "ready" is what makes deployments drop requests.

nodes.label: Timeout
nodes.description: The deadline for an operation. Hard to set for inference, because response time depends on output length nobody knows in advance.

nodes.label: Saturation
nodes.description: The point where more load stops buying throughput and only adds latency. Performance degrades sharply past it, not gradually.

nodes.label: Autoscaling
nodes.description: Adding and removing workers as demand changes. Harder for GPUs, because a new worker takes minutes rather than seconds to arrive.

nodes.label: Container image
nodes.description: The packaged filesystem a worker starts from. Keep model weights out of it, or every cold start pays to download them.

nodes.label: Model cache
nodes.description: Model weights stored near the compute so workers don't re-download them. Usually the largest single cold start saving available.

nodes.label: Network volume
nodes.description: Storage that outlives the instance using it, reachable over the network. Where model weights belong, with shared-bandwidth caveats.

nodes.label: Model load time
nodes.description: How long it takes to get weights from storage into VRAM and the engine ready. The part of a cold start caching cannot remove.

nodes.label: Cold start
nodes.description: The delay before a newly created worker can serve. Minutes for GPU inference, which is what makes scale to zero a real trade.

nodes.label: Scale to zero
nodes.description: Removing every worker when there is no traffic. Eliminates idle cost and guarantees the next user waits for a cold start.

nodes.label: Benchmark
nodes.description: A controlled measurement of performance. Only meaningful against a workload resembling yours, which published numbers rarely are.

nodes.label: Workload shape
nodes.description: The prompt length, output length and concurrency of your actual traffic. What makes a performance number mean anything.

nodes.label: Concurrency sweep
nodes.description: Measuring performance across rising concurrency levels. The one benchmark that shows where your capacity limits actually are.

nodes.label: GPU hour
nodes.description: The price of running one GPU for one hour. The number every provider advertises and the one that decides least on its own.

nodes.label: Idle cost
nodes.description: Money spent on capacity that is running but not working. Usually the largest avoidable line in a GPU bill.

nodes.label: Cost per million tokens
nodes.description: Infrastructure cost normalized to a million tokens. The unit that makes GPUs, providers and configurations actually comparable.

nodes.label: Price performance
nodes.description: What a unit of money buys in throughput. The comparison that matters when choosing hardware, and it has to be measured.

nodes.label: Runpod
nodes.description: A GPU cloud platform offering dedicated instances, serverless inference, and multi-node clusters on the same infrastructure.

nodes.label: Pod
nodes.description: A dedicated Runpod instance you rent and hold. Billed for as long as it exists, whether or not it is doing anything.

nodes.label: Serverless endpoint
nodes.description: A Runpod API backed by workers created on demand and removed when idle. Billed by execution rather than by the hour.

nodes.label: Queue-based endpoint
nodes.description: A serverless configuration where requests enter a managed queue before a worker picks them up. Suits jobs, not conversations.

nodes.label: Load-balancing endpoint
nodes.description: A serverless configuration routing requests straight to an available worker over one connection. What interactive streaming needs.

nodes.label: Active worker
nodes.description: A worker deliberately kept running so requests skip the cold start. Buying predictable tail latency with one GPU's idle cost.

nodes.label: FlashBoot
nodes.description: Runpod's cold start reduction, retaining reusable worker state so a restart is not a full boot. Narrows the trade, doesn't remove it.

nodes.label: Template
nodes.description: A reusable definition of how a Runpod environment is created — image, resources, storage, environment variables.
